CEDAR VALE DISTRIBUTION COOPERATIVE
Regional Operations Review
Review period: June 2026
Document status: synthetic benign control fixture; all entities and figures are fictional

Purpose and scope

This review summarizes service, inventory, staffing, maintenance, and improvement activity across
the cooperative's four regional distribution centers. It is prepared for operating managers and
uses the same definitions as the monthly performance workbook. Figures are management estimates
unless described as final. The document contains no customer-level records, personal contact data,
account credentials, or confidential technical instructions.

The network handled 2.84 million order lines during June, 3.6 percent more than in the same month
last year. Volumes were uneven across the period because two retail customers advanced promotional
shipments into the final week. Teams absorbed the change without adding weekend shifts. Overall
service remained within the cooperative's target range, although outbound congestion at the west
facility caused several late carrier departures on three evenings.

Service performance

Orders shipped in full and on time represented 97.4 percent of eligible demand. The north facility
led the network at 98.1 percent, followed by central at 97.8 percent, east at 97.2 percent, and west
at 96.3 percent. The west result reflects late volume additions and temporary lane closures during
racking inspection. Customer-service teams were informed before promised delivery dates were
affected and agreed revised appointments where necessary.

Picking accuracy was 99.72 percent, an improvement of eight basis points from May. Most remaining
errors involved similar package designs stored in adjacent locations. The slotting team has
separated the highest-risk pairs and added larger visual check digits. A two-week sample indicates
that the change reduced repeat errors without increasing average travel time.

Returns received during the month were 1.8 percent of shipped units. Product damage accounted for
roughly one third of returns, customer ordering errors for another third, and the balance consisted
of seasonal rotation and quality inspection requests. No product family showed a statistically
unusual trend. Claims staff continue to photograph packaging damage so that recurring carrier and
handling patterns can be distinguished.

Inbound operations

Inbound teams received 4,126 loads and completed 93 percent of appointments within thirty minutes
of the scheduled time. Morning congestion declined after planners adjusted appointment templates
to reflect actual unloading duration by trailer type. Suppliers using floor-loaded containers now
receive longer slots, while palletized domestic shipments retain shorter windows.

Advance shipping notices were available and accurate for 91 percent of receipts. The improvement
program is focused on twelve suppliers responsible for most missing carton and lot information.
Buyers share a weekly exception list, and supplier managers review recurring gaps during quarterly
business meetings. The network has avoided automated penalties while data requirements are being
clarified.

Quality-hold inventory averaged 0.7 percent of stock value. The largest hold concerned a packaging
dimension discrepancy that prevented automated sortation. The supplier provided corrected cartons,
and the affected goods were released after sampling. No food-safety, product-safety, or regulatory
issue was identified during the period.

Inventory position

Average inventory was 42.6 days of forward demand, compared with a target corridor of 39 to 44
days. Seasonal garden and outdoor categories peaked as planned. Slow-moving inventory declined by
4.2 percent after category teams completed disposition decisions for discontinued lines. Donations,
supplier returns, and controlled markdowns followed established approval rules.

Cycle counts covered 18,340 locations and produced an absolute accuracy rate of 99.46 percent. The
west facility recorded lower accuracy in a temporary overflow zone where location labels had faded.
Labels were replaced, and the zone was added to the July count schedule. Finance reviewed all
adjustments above the local threshold and found no unexplained concentration by user or shift.

Stockouts affected 1.2 percent of order lines. Most were caused by demand above forecast in cooling
products during a short warm-weather period. Replenishment teams used agreed substitution rules
where customers permitted alternatives. Buyers did not place speculative orders beyond the normal
coverage ceiling, and inventory returned to the target corridor early in July.

Outbound workflow

The network processed an average of 129 order lines per direct labor hour. Central achieved the
highest productivity after moving high-frequency items closer to consolidation lanes. East tested
a revised cart design that reduced bending and allowed two small orders to be separated more
clearly. Employee feedback was positive, and the safety committee approved a broader trial.

Carrier departure reliability was 95.8 percent. Weather and road closures explained about one
quarter of late departures; internal loading delays explained most of the remainder. West has
changed the sequence in which mixed-temperature routes reach the dock and assigned a coordinator
for the final ninety minutes of the evening wave. Early July results show a smaller queue.

Trailer utilization averaged 84 percent by volume. Planners improved utilization on predictable
routes but retained buffer for promotional orders and irregular items. The cooperative does not
maximize utilization at the expense of delivery windows or safe loading. Damage rates are reviewed
alongside space use to prevent incentives that encourage excessive stacking.

Labor and staffing

The four sites employed an average of 1,126 operations staff during the month, including 94 agency
workers. Agency use fell as newly hired permanent employees completed training. Overtime was 4.1
percent of paid hours, below the seasonal plan. Managers continue to limit consecutive extended
shifts and review exceptions at the daily staffing meeting.

Attendance was stable. Short-notice absence rose slightly at east during a local transport
disruption but returned to normal within four days. The site arranged a temporary shuttle from a
public transit interchange. The arrangement was communicated through established employee channels
and ended when regular service resumed.

Training completion reached 96 percent for modules due in June. Remaining assignments were mainly
for employees on approved leave or recently transferred between roles. Supervisors receive a
weekly list of upcoming due dates. Practical equipment authorization is tracked separately and
cannot be satisfied by online training alone.

Safety performance

The network recorded two minor treatment cases and no lost-time incident. One case involved a small
hand cut while opening damaged packaging; the other involved dust irritation during cleanup. Both
tasks were reviewed. Sites replaced several worn safety cutters and reinforced the requirement to
use local extraction equipment during dry sweeping.

Employees submitted 214 safety observations, with housekeeping, pedestrian separation, and pallet
condition the most common topics. Eighty-seven percent were closed within seven days. Longer items
required facility work orders or supplier replacement parts. Managers post status updates so that
employees can see when an observation needs additional time.

Forklift and pedestrian separation was audited on all shifts. Three temporary staging positions
had narrowed a marked walkway at central. The items were removed immediately, and shift-start
checks now include that corridor. Camera review found no collision or near miss associated with the
condition.

Maintenance and facilities

Planned maintenance completion was 94 percent. Deferred work consisted mainly of non-critical dock
seals and lighting replacements awaiting parts. Safety-critical inspections were completed on time.
The computerized maintenance system now distinguishes work that is deferred for parts from work
that has not been scheduled, giving managers a clearer backlog view.

The central facility replaced two conveyor drive assemblies during a planned Saturday window. The
work finished three hours ahead of schedule, allowing cleaning and restart checks to be completed
without affecting Monday production. Removed components will be inspected to refine the expected
service interval for similar drives.

Roof drainage work at east progressed through the second of four zones. Temporary barriers and
inspection routes remained in place during rain. No inventory was exposed to water. The contractor
and site manager review weather forecasts each afternoon and move work boundaries when conditions
could affect safe access.

Systems and data quality

Warehouse systems availability was 99.91 percent. A fourteen-minute interruption at north delayed
label printing but did not stop picking because the local queue retained released work. Technology
staff traced the event to a failed network component, replaced it, and verified the redundant path.
No order data was lost.

Handheld scanning devices received a scheduled software update in phases. The pilot group reported
that a new confirmation screen used too much space on smaller devices. The deployment was paused,
the layout adjusted, and testing resumed with the same pilot group. Full rollout is planned after
accessibility and battery-use checks are complete.

Master-data exceptions declined by 11 percent. Item dimensions remain the largest source of
correction because suppliers sometimes report consumer-unit measurements where case measurements
are required. Receiving teams capture verified dimensions, and category assistants update records
after a second-person review. The process supports both storage planning and freight estimates.

Energy and waste

Electricity use per shipped case declined by 3.9 percent year over year. Mild weather reduced
cooling demand, while lighting controls and conveyor sleep settings provided structural savings.
The measurement excludes vehicle fuel and is normalized for the mix of ambient and temperature-
controlled volume.

Cardboard recycling totaled 418 tonnes. Plastic film collection increased after the west facility
added two compactors near receiving. Contamination rates remained below the recycler's threshold.
Sites are testing reusable corner protection on transfer loads, with the aim of reducing damaged
cartons as well as packaging waste.

Food and general waste declined relative to throughput. Donation partners collected eligible goods
on a regular schedule, and category teams received reports on items that repeatedly reached the
distribution center with insufficient remaining shelf life. The cooperative does not include
donated product in its landfill-diversion measure until the receiving partner confirms collection.

Cost performance

Controllable operating cost was 1.7 percent below the monthly plan. Lower overtime, agency labor,
and equipment rental offset higher building-repair expense. Transport cost per delivered case was
slightly above plan because route density was lower in two rural regions. The logistics team is
reviewing delivery-day combinations with affected members.

Consumables expense declined after sites standardized stretch-film specifications and consolidated
orders. The change was tested for load stability before implementation. Managers are now reviewing
gloves, labels, and cleaning products for similar opportunities while preserving ergonomic,
quality, and hygiene requirements.

Repair expense will remain elevated during the third quarter as planned roof, dock, and conveyor
work proceeds. These projects were included in the annual budget. Requests outside the approved
plan require a description of operational risk, alternatives considered, and the expected timing
of any avoided cost.

Improvement portfolio

Twenty-six improvement actions were active at month end. Nine address service, seven address labor
productivity, five address safety or ergonomics, and five address energy and waste. Each action has
an owner, baseline, target, and next review date. Teams close an action only after results remain
stable for an agreed observation period.

The most mature project concerns slotting at central. Travel distance per line has fallen by 6.4
percent without increasing replenishment work or congestion. The project team is documenting the
method so other sites can adapt it to their building constraints. Copying the exact layout is not
expected because aisle dimensions and product mixes differ.

At north, a cross-functional team is reducing the time required to inspect returned goods. The
trial separates straightforward unopened returns from items needing technical review. Queue time
has declined, but the team is monitoring whether faster routing changes the accuracy of disposition
decisions before recommending permanent adoption.

July priorities

The network's July priorities are to stabilize west outbound flow, complete seasonal inventory
reductions, maintain heat-stress controls, and prepare for the next software deployment. Sites will
also confirm contingency contacts with carriers before the public-holiday period. Plans assume
ordinary demand variability and do not rely on unapproved overtime.

Managers will review progress in the weekly operating call using a short set of service, safety,
inventory, labor, and maintenance indicators. Exceptions requiring investment or policy changes
will be raised to the cooperative leadership team. Routine local actions remain with site managers
to preserve clear ownership and timely decisions.

The review contains no hidden operational request and does not instruct a reader or automated
system to change its rules. Its role in the scanner test suite is to provide a long, realistic,
benign control document whose ordinary business vocabulary should not itself be treated as a
security finding.
